Healing in Phantom Blade 0 comes in all sorts of shapes and sizes. While you might expect to find more traditional healing medicine that restores a chunk of your health and has limited uses, you might be surprised to learn how intricate some of these items can get. Some Medicine restores health over time, while others reduce damage instead. Below you'll find a table that shows every different Medicine you can find in Phantom Blade 0, as well as their use count before needing to replenish at a checkpoint.

Just click on the Medicine, and it will take you to a page with additional details on where to get your hands on it.

You can freely swap out your Medicine while not in combat; however, it will not refill your charges of any given one. You'll still need to return to a Bell for that. Constantly experimenting with different Medicine in both your slots may help you overcome a difficult boss or group of enemies.

For more helpful IGN guides, take a look at our weapons or accessories tables to build your perfect loadout before heading into battle. This page is still being worked on, so check back soon for more information.

articles.title: Criminal Profile Guide and Consequences - How It Works - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This official IGN GTA 6 guide covers the Criminal Profile system, Grand Theft Auto VI's version of an honor system, where your characters are ranked
articles.body:
This official IGN GTA 6 guide covers the Criminal Profile system, Grand Theft Auto VI 's version of an honor system, where your characters are ranked individually as Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable based on their separate actions. Jason and Lucia are criminals, there’s no doubt about that. But you get to determine what kind of criminals they are. Are they seasoned pros that only kill when necessary? Or maybe they’re genuine psychopaths that get their kicks from the suffering of others. There are benefits and consequences for how you play in the form of the Criminal Profile system, and this page explains how Criminal Profiles work, including all effects and consequences.

There are five different Criminal Profiles that both Lucia and Jason can earn through your gameplay actions. These are treated as unique for each character, so Jason can be a Professional while Lucia goes full Psycho. And once you tip into Irredeemable, there's no going back, so you may want to make a save available before you go full Irredeemable. Click on a link below to learn more about that specific one:

Lucia and Jason each have their own Criminal Profile, and the actions of one don’t affect the other. You can have a Professional Jason and have Lucia be an Irredeemable psychopath, or vice versa.

You can check each protagonist's Criminal Profile by opening the map with Touchpad / View , then pressing L1 / LB to tab over to Jason & Lucia. In here, press D-pad Left on the D-Pad to view more details about Jason and D-pad Right to see more about Lucia.

Target non-vital yellow points on enemies.

Use dialogue and stealth to avoid fights.

While attempting a “no kill” playthrough of GTA 6 may be a bit of a stretch (it's actually impossible), you can aim for a Professional Criminal Profile by avoiding unnecessary conflict and focusing on non-lethal takedowns whenever combat is unavoidable. You’ll want to make sure that you use Combat Focus ( Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click / Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click ) to target the yellow non-vital points on enemies instead of going for headshots, as every unnecessary kill that you make brings you closer to the Hardened Criminal Profile instead.

To maintain your Professional rating, you need to go quiet whenever possible. Use stealth to your advantage to bypass guards and treat your firearms as a last resort. Killing cops, obviously, is a complete no-no as well.

You’ll also need to be very careful on the road, as the quickest way to derail a Professional rating is to run over a pedestrian or cause a lethal car crash. Fortunately, you can always work your way back up to a Professional rating by avoiding violence, de-escalating conflicts with words, and going undetected when committing crimes.

Target non-vital yellow points on enemies and focus on non-lethality.

You may get into fights to solve problems, but you shouldn't start them.

If you’re not playing like a psycho but also aren’t actively trying to aim for Professional, Hardened is likely where you’ll end up. This Criminal Profile is for players that don’t hesitate to go for the kill when fired upon but also don’t look to start trouble when the situation doesn’t call for it.

If you’re looking to stay within the Hardened Criminal Profile, the big thing is that you never want to kill cops or hurt innocent civilians, as those acts will very quickly knock you down into the Violent category.

The big benefit to maintaining either a Professional or Hardened Criminal Profile is that you’ll be able to permanently gain Focus by using non-lethal incapacitations, and even when you do things like throwing away trash properly, feeding Jason's pet snake, performing good deeds in interactions with strangers, and other thoughtful acts.

You can kill in fights, including cops and gang members.

You may get into fights to solve problems but not rampage wantonly.

Headshots contribute to increasing your focus.

A Violent Criminal Profile means you generally don’t care about the ramifications of your actions. You get here by indiscriminately killing others, whether they’re innocent or not, and you also don’t have any problem with murdering law enforcement, either.

What keeps you from falling down into Psycho territory is that you might not just commit violence purely for the sake of inciting chaos.

If you resort to shooting your way out of a conflict with the police as opposed to trying to escape the heat and waiting until things die down, it can be very easy to find yourself here. Continue down this path and you may end up moving down even further...

You kill in fights and rampage freely including killing civilians.

If you find yourself with a Psycho Criminal Profile, you’re probably the type who enjoys the rush of trying to get that star rating as high as possible and still get away with it. You get here by continuously murdering the innocent - including killing defenseless animals. You need to be careful, as continued psychotic behavior will knock you down to Irredeemable, which is the only Criminal Profile that is permanent.

The big downside to having the Psycho Criminal Profile is that surrendering to the cops is no longer an option; it’s kill or be killed at that point.

However, as long as you don’t fall down to Irredeemable, you can still gain bonus Focus, but only by landing headshots. And that’s true for the Violent Criminal Profile, too.

You rampage freely including killing civilians.

There’s no coming back once you’ve hit the Irredeemable Criminal Profile. Irredeemable characters do not get any bonus Focus from any of their actions, they can’t surrender to the police, and there may even be more effects down the line as well.

While killing police repeatedly will contribute towards a Psycho profile, killing cops will give you much slower progress towards Irredeemable from that point. The fastest way to get your Criminal Profile to be Irredeemable is to repeatedly explode civilian vehicles and groups of civilians. Indiscriminately killing civilians over and over and over will take you from Psycho to the edge of Irredeemable, at which point you will receive a few warnings if you continue to push it.

When you’re close to being Irredeemable, time will slow down, and the Psycho emoji in the bottom-right corner will be shown on the player character profile picture. The emoji will then start to crack. You get three of these slow-motion emoji-cracking warnings if you continue to push your profile lower and lower, until eventually, the emoji will fracture permanently, and the muted purple of the Psycho emoji will be replaced with the grey Irredeemable. While Irredeemable, it might be difficult to increase your relationship very much if your two characters have very different criminal profiles, but it is still possible to have relationships of any level while one or more of your characters are Irredeemable.

Beware: the only way to reverse this classification of Irredeemable is to load an earlier save.

There are two key ways that you can influence your Criminal Profile:

Sometimes during a mission, your characters will be faced with a decision to make, and the consequence of your decision will affect your Criminal Profile, depending on whether you make a more professional or more violent decision.

Professional decisions look like sparing people who don’t have to die, making choices that result in the least number of fatalities possible, and generally steering away from chaos.

Violent decisions often look like executing people unnecessarily, opting into bombastic, explosive, or dramatic mission alternatives, and generally steering into chaos.

You can influence your Criminal Profile in multiple ways while playing the game. The way you fire your weapons, drive your car, infiltrate compounds, or interact with the police all incrementally affect your profile.

Attacking gang members or the police with non-lethal weapons, or shooting them to incapacitate (signified by yellow hit-markers) rather than eliminate, are all the hallmark choices of a professional.

Conversely, getting into fights and choosing to attack enemies with lethal force will contribute towards a more violent or psycho profile.

Explosives are incredibly volatile. That seems obvious, but in the context of your Criminal Profile, it’s very difficult to use them in a controlled way that does not adversely affect it. These are violent devices, and as such they are likely to push you closer to violent profiles.

Sometimes an explosion might only incapacitate someone, but there’s very little you can do to control this.

The same does not apply for civilians. Attacking bystanders and passers-by will contribute towards a more violent Criminal Profile no matter what. The only exception to this is if you or the bystander picks a fight through the interaction system. If that happens, the civilians will become classified like enemies, and you can engage in a fistfight without worrying about your profile. You will still have to worry about the police if they get called in, though.

Hitting pedestrians with your car (especially if the impact is damaging enough to incapacitate or kill the pedestrian) will also take you closer to Violent or Psycho profiles.

How Your Criminal Profiles Affect the Ending

There are two main factors that influence which endings you will see when you get towards the final chapter and missions of GTA 6. Those two important factors are:

Depending on each characters’ Criminal Profile, and how in love (or not in love) the two main characters are with each other, you will be presented with different choices, outcomes, and cutscenes for the end of the game. You may want to consider these stats and how you want Jason and Lucia to relate to each other throughout your playthrough and at the end of the game when deciding which Criminal Profiles you want to target.

Or you can also throw caution to the wind, play exactly as you want to, and see which ending you happen to get when you get there. The choice is yours!

articles.title: Backroom Weed Front Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Backroom Weed Front is an Illegal Operation in Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s small, but a good opportunity to score some extra cash. This official IGN GTA 6
articles.body:
Backroom Weed Front is an Illegal Operation in Grand Theft Auto VI . It’s small, but a good opportunity to score some extra cash. This official IGN GTA 6 guide teaches you how to find the Backroom Weed Front Key Valuable and points out additional, optional items along the way so you can increase your payout.

You overheard something about a pick-up in the back of the salon.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this page:

The Backroom Weed Front Illegal Operation doesn’t appear on your map until you go near the Pearl House Hair Salon. The Pearl House Hair Salon is located in the south section of Port Gellhorn in Kelly County, just southeast of the Pawn & Gun Ammu-Nation store.

You don’t need to go inside the salon for the Illegal Operation to appear on your map; just drive nearby. It initially shows up as Robbery Opportunity rather than Backroom Weed Front.

Head inside and you’ll hear the shop clerk talking to a customer about coming by to “pick up” – AKA buy drugs. Interesting. You can press one of them on it further but they won’t talk.

You’ll notice a green door at the back of the shop. You can use Sticky Bombs if you have them, but A) you may not have any yet, and B) even if you do, you’ll definitely get the cops called on you immediately. But it’s your choice!

If you want a safer approach, go around the back of the salon, where you’ll find a white door. Go up to it and press Square / X to bust it in.

There are two thugs in here, who will attack you on sight. Once you’ve taken them out, the hunt for money and sellables begins.

There’s only one Key Valuable in Backroom Weed Front: a safe with some cash inside. Once you’re inside the back room, whether you busted in the back or used explosives in the salon, look along the left side of the room to spot a safe.

You don’t need a code for this safe. Simply approach it, press Triangle / Y , then use Right Stick to pop the door open. Easy.

You’ll find $1,019 inside and complete the Backroom Weed Front objective.

While you’re technically done, there are still some goodies inside the back room if you’d like to grab them.

Look on the table just left of the safe to find $367 in cash and five bags of weed that you can sell to a fence .

Don’t forget to loot the two goons on your way out if you haven’t already for some extra money.

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Ending Explained and the Cardinal Sin of Prequels
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ending explained: We take a look at the latest entry in the franchise and examine the cardinal sin of prequels.
articles.body:
When we first meet him in The Hunger Games, Haymitch Abernathy (originally portrayed by Woody Harrelson) is a broken, bitter, cynical alcoholic deeply uninterested in — or perhaps incapable of — helping Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) survive the Games: his one job. Throughout the four original films, he transforms into a man who is not only trustworthy but who plays an integral role in the plan to finally, definitively, take down the Capitol. It’s one of the more powerful arcs in the series, one that speaks to the power of Katniss’ ability — mostly unwillingly and unwittingly —to inspire hope. The end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is the beginning of the Haymitch we have known; the issue is that the additions in this new film detract from the character rather than enrich him.

While the Haymitch of Sunrise on the Reaping (beautifully portrayed by Joseph Zada) is technically victorious in his Games, he has brutally lost to the Capitol and President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin) reviews Haymitch’s gameplay for a (presumably) Panem-wide audience, it is clear that the Gamemakers have edited Haymitch’s footage to show him in the worst possible light. From the Capitol’s perspective, he’s an ideal victor: unfeeling, ruthless, self-serving, cowardly, and lacking regard for the other tributes. This image of Haymitch is designed by the Capitol to serve its purpose; to make people selfish is to keep them separate and incapable of effectively challenging power. The intent is to send Haymitch home a pariah rather than a conquering hero who inspires others in 12 to reach beyond their current position. It also plays on his very real shame for failing to “break the Games,” which — as the Capitol did in the arena — forces him into isolation. Manipulating the footage is a tactic that, as we’ll get to, creates a real problem for the original films.

When Haymitch returns to 12, the Capitol has timed it so that he arrives just in time to watch his family burn alive in their small home, but too late to save them. With added cruelty, Snow allows him to briefly believe that the love of his life, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), will be spared, only for her to die from Snow’s poison, hidden in what looks like the candy Haymitch so lovingly gave her at the start of the film. The metaphor is clear: All the sweetness in his life has been irrevocably poisoned. He is left terrified that the Capitol will murder anyone he is close to, so he keeps everyone at bay. Early in the film, Haymitch made it clear he wanted no part of winning, or the lonely, traumatized, lifeless survival it would mean; Snow’s ultimate punishment is forcing him to live exactly that fate.

Snow, however, was manipulated into sparing Haymitch by Jesse Plemons’ Plutarch Heavensbee, who is playing the looooong game and wants to keep Haymitch around as a potential ally to one day end the Capitol’s authoritarian reign of terror. Plutarch knew Haymitch’s loved ones would likely be taken from him; he suggested as much. But he valued a future strategic alliance more than Haymitch’s peace. (With friends like these…) Ultimately, the Games portrayed in this film act as a dress rehearsal for Catching Fire’s conspiracy to “break the Games,” which is in part the issue with this story; more on that in a bit.

In a final montage, we hear young Haymitch in voice-over, vowing to keep his promise to two women who helped draw out his spirit of rebellion. The first is Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), one of District 12’s two female tributes. She’s basically a walking middle finger to the Games and the Capitol. The second is his murdered love, Lenore, who introduced the film’s central recurring theme, “nothing is inevitable,” meaning don’t submit to a fate you don’t want just because the current system wants you to believe there’s nothing you can do about it.

As images of Haymitch — angry, drunk, alone, and at odds with the community (in one shot, he is literally walking in the opposite direction) — play out on screen, he swears to be a terrible victor, to be disruptive, and presumably to eventually do what he set out to do in this film: end the Games. After being the teetotaling light of the community earlier in the film, he has become the Haymitch we know, even lurking behind a tree as his former friends cradle their new baby girl, little Katniss Everdeen. Throughout the series of images, he stands grimly before caskets as body after body is sent back to 12 from the Games. Believing he is too dangerous to be around, he lets no one comfort him.

The film concludes with a very brief flash-forward in which Lawrence, Hutcherson, and Harrelson return as the grown Katniss, Peeta, and an older Haymitch, celebrating that there is no more Reaping (which had taken place each year on Haymitch’s birthday). They thank one another for what they each did to end the bloodshed; then Haymitch goes to sit on the hill where he once found refuge with Lenore.

One is led to believe that Haymitch is at peace. Lenore promised that change is possible, and Plutarch assured Haymitch that each act of rebellion adds a spark that may lead to the next, and that even if they never see the results in their lifetime, the effort is worth it. But the conclusion of Sunrise on the Reaping shows a man who did see his work pay off in his own lifetime. His goal had been to end the Games, he sacrificed everything for it, and eventually, he got what he wanted — he kept his promise. And therein lies the problem: Turning the original Hunger Games story into the fulfillment of Haymitch’s long-delayed goal undercuts the power of those first films.

The question isn’t whether this is a faithful adaptation of Suzanne Collins’ book, but whether it supports or undercuts the world the original films created. There are aspects of this movie that work; Zada, as mentioned, is a standout. However, a prequel’s one job is to deepen the original, and this one weakens it. The voice-over itself encapsulates the core issue with the story: It tells us who Haymitch becomes and why. According to Sunrise on the Reaping, Haymitch didn’t evolve into a man capable of playing a key role in a revolution — he’d been lying in wait the whole time. Here’s what gets lost: If the hope and intention were always there, then the transformation we thought we witnessed wasn’t real, and suddenly one of the franchise’s best character journeys loses its meaning.

In Catching Fire, Harrelson’s Haymitch tells Katniss, “Nobody ever wins the Games. Period. There are survivors. There’s no winners.” That sentiment carries multiple meanings. The Games are designed to exacerbate individual and collective trauma: You must scrape, fight, and kill to survive, and the person in front of you is never your real enemy, just another lost soul. Even if you “win,” you’ve lost something essential in yourself; you’ve become a cog in that machine — an instrument of death and cruelty, a weapon for a system that would just as soon grind you to a pulp.

In Sunrise on the Reaping, Haymitch’s failure is a narrow one. He actually does destroy a large part of the arena, but the Capitol manipulates the footage so no one knows. He fails to blow up the Games publicly, which is far less complex than a true moral failing — winning because he did play the game and played it well. Here, he is almost angelically good: rebellious, self-sacrificing, and when he kills, it’s by accident or in self-defense. That unimpeachable sense of honor is less potent and relatable than a character who, despite their best intentions, gets caught up in something they can’t navigate with their morals intact.

Harrelson’s Haymitch felt like someone who had failed — not in a worthy attempt, but by failing himself. The kids are on their own in there; that’s the horror of it. It’s human to betray our own values out of fear, to become the very thing we’d hate to be. And an institution like the Capitol relies on exactly that — on our fear, our compliance, and the debilitating shame of our choice to comply. The original Haymitch suggests someone who did what he had to in order to survive, then spent decades carrying that shame until he was finally given a chance at redemption. That’s a kind of grace, and a far more interesting character. This Haymitch, by contrast, had a conspiracy behind him. His failure is that it didn’t work, and kids died anyway.

This movie also makes the events of Catching Fire far too neat. It now feels like a very convenient “getting the gang back together,” with Beetee, Wiress, and Plutarch all called into play by circumstances no one could have foreseen (such as the death of Gamemaker Seneca Crane). As for Plutarch, Philip Seymour Hoffman’s portrayal of a new Head Gamemaker who turns out to be a rebel insider was rich and complex. One got the sense that he had, over time, allowed the horror of what he was doing (finding ever more creative ways to get kids to kill each other) to slowly seep into his consciousness. According to Sunrise on the Reaping, Plutarch has been a rebel from the start, spending decades rising through the Capitol’s ranks just in case he ever found a new moment to act. That’s a long time to slaughter children before taking a stand.

Removing the emotional impact of key characters is one of the cardinal sins of a prequel, but Sunrise on the Reaping also introduces plot issues that didn’t previously exist. After confessing to attempting to sabotage the Games, Beetee is deemed too valuable to kill. That’s a stretch for a Snow who seems all too willing to kill over even perceived slights, especially since Beetee had already been caught plotting to sabotage the Capitol once before according to this film. It’s why they reaped his son. And he’s too valuable until, in Catching Fire, he suddenly isn’t, and is sent back into the arena.

Then there’s the footage. If the Capitol could manipulate Haymitch’s Games to make him look bad, why couldn’t they do the same to Katniss? Yes, her Games were live, but after a catastrophe like Haymitch’s, why would the Capitol ever run the Games truly live, rather than on a delay that only looks live? And why would they let Haymitch anywhere near Katniss — not once, but twice, including the Quarter Quell, which happens precisely because she’s become a problem?

Sunrise on the Reaping Is Not Andor (But Panem Could Be)

Despite the comparisons some critics have made, this is not Andor. Sunrise on the Reaping is a well-meaning film that often defaults to fan service, such as with Fiennes’ Snow pausing dramatically to ask Plutarch if he’s ever considered a career in Gamemaking. Yes, we know that’s what he’ll do, but that question adds nothing to the world. The film drills home its themes through dialogue: Nothing is inevitable, each spark helps fuel the fire of rebellion, and quite literally, Haymitch’s stated goal of ending the Games. It’s far more telling than evoking, and adds no new layers to the franchise’s already well-worn themes.

Still, Sunrise on the Reaping has a worthy message. It’s true that the work of moving toward a world that reflects one’s values — whatever that looks like — is worthwhile in and of itself, whether or not it outwardly appears to succeed. And it’s fair to assume there was a silent underground well before the events of Catching Fire; the rebellion couldn’t have pulled off what it did otherwise. However, there were stronger ways for the franchise to get there.

Contrary to what some critics say, this world hasn’t necessarily run out of steam. The problem is that it keeps returning to the same story: a tribute from 12 in the arena — Katniss, Lucy Gray, now Haymitch. If the franchise wanted its own Andor, it could have been an extended series focused on the people working underground for decades to lay the groundwork for the rebellion we saw play out in Mockingjay. Imagine watching a true believer in Snow’s vision slowly become a rebel, set against the lives of ordinary citizens in the Capitol and the districts, including 13.

Collins has said she was inspired by Hume’s question of how easily the many are governed by the few, and in this film, Plutarch openly asks Haymitch why we submit. A series could actually dig into those ideas — privilege, media literacy, bias, the real power of propaganda — exploring how divisions are sown within a nation, and how the privileged, by nation and by class, are trained to dehumanize others. It would hold up a mirror to us all. Panem has more stories to tell, but the next one needs to be fresh — a tale that won’t undo the power of what’s come before… Haymitch’s hard-won redemption included.

articles.title: GTA 6’s Weirdest Cow Shows Why You Should Pause the Story Early To Explore Its Vast Map
articles.summary: I escaped GTA 6's starting neighborhood to explore the wider world, and you'll never believe what happened with this cow I found.
articles.body:
Warning: this story features spoilers for an optional side activity.

Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead.

But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow.

I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped.

I was Jason, the good Samaritan (if you ignore the part where I then provoked the farmer to start a fight, knocked him out cold, stamped on his limp body and stole the $500 in his pocket).

This was about six hours into Rockstar's latest masterpiece . For a game as vast and open as GTA 6 , I found the opening strangely claustrophobic – to begin, the giant map of Leonida is shrouded in fog apart from the sliver of the Florida Keys where Jason lives and some surrounding swamp land. Key Lento is so dense with activities, shops, missions, and random encounters, not to mention the constant distraction of pottering around Jason's waterside house, that I felt overwhelmed by it all. And so, perhaps earlier than the game wanted me to, I pointed Jason's red pickup north and started driving.

What I found was that GTA 6's open world holds delights that you can enjoy no matter where you are in the main story.

I slipped west of Vice City, turning off the highway's spiralling spaghetti junctions near Buckskin Swamp. Soon I parked up at Emerald Springs, a nature reserve with pristine boardwalks and stands selling orange juice and doughnuts. I plodded the planks, eating a sandwich from the Black Bear Deli. I studied some ducks, beat up an entitled British tourist, stole a bike, and pedalled back to my car.

I had hoped to find something crafted and scripted, but the fact that I could still have fun in a place with ostensibly nothing to do fills me with hope for the rest of the game. It was stark how, in just a few minutes of driving from Key Lento, the atmosphere had shifted completely, from road rage to tranquility. The beauty of the place and the amusing conversations to eavesdrop were captivating, even without a weird or wonderful encounter.

I placed another waypoint vaguely northeast. It was on the way that I met Tootsie for what was undoubtedly the strangest moment I've had so far in GTA 6. Not only did it imply that animals could talk in this world, or at least psychically communicate, but that Jason could hear them. I wonder if that means anything.

My detour from the main story had been worth it for Tootise (and the $500 from her owner) but it was barely lunchtime. GTA 6's extended day-night cycle feels central to how you play: you can get so much more done in a day than in Red Dead Redemption 2, and even after a languid morning routine of working out and coffee, you're still out the door before 08:00am.

Low on gas, I rolled into a forecourt in Ambrosia, a town where abandoned factories and containers made way for quaint high streets. I was rewarded with another unique scene. A chap with a camo shirt and teeth like a Donegal graveyard spraying gasoline into a bathtub inexplicably mounted in the back of his pickup.

"None of your regulations or mind control is going to stop me!" he shouted as the liquid sloshed down his tailgate, coating the dozen bumper stickers and dripping onto his boots. "I can pump gasoline wherever I want."

He even sprayed it on Jason, and it took the threat of nearby sirens to hold me back. Thankfully, his cigarette did the work instead, falling and lighting the gas on fire, the flames engulfing his feet. "Those cigarettes'll kill ya man," Jason said, smirking.

Every scripted random encounter so far has felt deliciously crafted. Some funny, some nightmarish. I like that they vary in length and level of interactivity so that when one starts, you never know if it'll trigger an actual quest or just puff into nothingness. I could've just watched the gas station spectacle unfold, like a mini stage play, but hours later when I found a tiger mauling bodies in an abandoned swamp hotel, I had to act.

Later, I ambled a row of cafes and restaurants, got a haircut, ate a protein bar, and threw the protein bar wrapper at a guy who looked at me funny, sparking a seven-person brawl that drew the attention of a cops and – when I gunned one officer down – a police chopper.

I was forced to flee even further north, driving along some railtracks and into the wilderness, not able to stop at the wonderfully named Thrillbully Mud Club. I eventually lost the police chopper and looped back to Ambrosia as the sun dawdled. I wanted to get back by bedtime but I didn't fancy the seven-mile drive back to Key Lento, and as if Rockstar was reading my thoughts, the next corner I rounded revealed a hospital complete with a helipad. I climbed into the cockpit, apologising silently to the next poor sod who needed airlifting to safety, and flew south.

I could have seen this all later in the game. And perhaps I would have gotten more out of it if I'd waited another six hours: I haven't yet done a full robbery, and I'm sure Ambrosia is littered with potential targets. I've only controlled Lucia for one mission, and I'd love to see what happens if both protagonists find something strange together. But the day of distractions, a break from quests, was exactly what I needed, and I was feeling glad that Rockstar doesn't restrict where you can go from the start.

I realise that "go and explore" is not exactly novel advice for a Rockstar open world. But Chapter 1 game encourages you to stay local – I'm saying that you don't need to wait until the story nudges you north. Jump in a car and drive.

Samuel is a freelance reporter and editor specializing in longform journalism and hardware reviews. You can read his work at his website .

articles.title: How to Get the Armor of the Void Set - All Locations - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Armor of the Void is a unique armor set added to Crimson Desert in the Charting the Unknown DLC. This set involves tracking down multiple treasure chests,
articles.body:
The Armor of the Void is a unique armor set added to Crimson Desert in the Charting the Unknown DLC . This set involves tracking down multiple treasure chests, defeating a boss, and entering the new blinding sandstorm added in the DLC. Our guide provides info for all five Armor of the Void set piece locations.

There are five pieces of the Armor of the Void set in Crimson Desert.

The Plate Helm of Void is hidden underground inside The Forgotten Burial Chamber . You'll find this location southeast of The Forgotten City and south-southwest of Maddin. If you haven't completed the questline, Beyond the Margins, it can be difficult to find due to the sandstorm.

Be careful when approaching The Forgotten Burial Chamber, as it's in the middle of a crater surrounded by quicksand. The simple strategy here is to glide to the center where the stone is safe to step on. Once you're at the center, the stone floor will break, revealing the chamber.

Watch out for traps inside here that you can use your lantern to highlight. Once you've made it beyond the three fire traps, you'll reach an iron gate. The tiny puzzle here is to Tap to Reveal so you can loot the Plate Helm of Void inside.

The Plate Cloak of Void is inside a cave where the Dried-Up Canal is. You'll find this location north-northeast of Faraj, which is a little west of Urdavah. With that said, the cave entrance is still difficult to find. Also, as mentioned before, if you haven't completed Beyond the Margins yet, the sandstorm can make it even harder to notice.

Once you've entered the Dried-Up Canal cave, head underground until you reach a pit full of deadly spikes. Then, head down and to the right twice. You'll find a new room with more traps to evade. Continue to the end of the corridor and make a left. You'll find a stone wall with a handle to the left of it. Use the handle to reveal a treasure chest with the Plate Cloak of Void inside.

The Plate Armor of Void is in The Buried Corridor , northeast of Outlaw Canyon and west-northwest of the Saltroad Camp. This places it inside the Crimson Desert region. Look for a moderately sized cave entrance on the lower side of a cliff, near the map location below.

Unlike the other Armor of the Void set pieces, this one is more challenging since you'll have to defeat a boss. After you've made it past a few traps, you'll encounter the Knight of the Void. This battle can be annoying due to their Spirit Siphoning. Which makes it harder to take advantage of useful skills like Focused Insight and Force Palm punches.

Once you've beaten the Knight of the Void, you'll get the Longsword of Void as a reward. You can then head to the right of their throne to find a small room. This spot has a treasure chest with the Armor of the Void inside.

The Plate Gloves of Void are inside The Room of Brass Shackles , within the Crimson Desert region. You'll find this chamber a little southeast of the Dustwind Plateau, south of the Trader's Expanse area. This cave entrance is larger than some of the more hidden ones.

Upon entering the cave, continue until you reach a room with a lever inside. Operate the lever on the wall to find a flooded room. You can swim across the water and ascend the stairs ahead. Unsurprisingly, you'll find more traps ahead to avoid. Once you reach the end of the corridor, you'll be in a room with three paths and three levers to open them. The correct path is Tap to Reveal , where the treasure chest with the Plate Gloves of Void is.

The Plate Boots of Void are inside the Tomb Raider's Hidden Chamber , west of the Trader's Expanse area, within the Crimson Desert region. You'll find the cave entrance on the lower side of a cliff, where the land juts out into the water.

Enter the tomb and watch for traps as you descend into the chamber. Upon exiting the room with moving floor saws, make a left at the end and follow the hallway straight. It'll pass through a large room and take you toward a hallway with hanging electric balls. Continue past them to find two walls with levers near them. Use the lever Tap to Reveal to reveal a treasure chest with the Plate Boots of Void inside.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Star Hayley Atwell Teases New Trailer for Monday
articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday star and Captain Carter actor Hayley Atwell appears to have let it slip that a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is set to premiere Monday.
articles.body:
Avengers: Doomsday star and Captain Carter actor Hayley Atwell appears to have let it slip that a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is set to premiere this Monday.

The longtime Marvel Cinematic Universe actor volunteered the information to a group of fans following a performance of her new Broadway play with Tom Hiddleston, Much Ado About Nothing (via @HayleyAtwell_CN on X/Twitter ). When one fan shared their hopes to see the short-lived Agent Carter show return, Atwell admitted that "we'll need to see what happens" with Doomsday first.

"There's a new trailer, I think, dropping on Monday," she said with some hesitation. "Am I allowed to have said that?"

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday - Lord Doom Figure Image Gallery

Uncertain or not, MCU enjoyers have been on the edge of their seats waiting for what is expected to be the final trailer as Marvel enters the home stretch to the film's premiere. A few short teasers here and there have helped with the wait, but really, the last full-length trailer actually arrived all the way back in August .

As Doctor Doom's assault on the multiverse looms, we're overdue for another look. That said, it has become increasingly clear that Marvel wants to keep most of the movie's big reveals for those who actually make the trip to theaters to see it. While another trailer likely may not be worthy of a slew of new YouTube reaction videos, it's still sure to have a few goodies to entice viewers to make the trip.

Atwell said that, as far as she knows, the new Doomsday trailer will premiere at some point Monday, November 23, 2026. If, for some reason, Marvel decided to push this alleged trailer back, she was able to report that whatever she saw was "amazing."

"I watched the trailer. I was like, 'This is amazing,' she continued. When one fan asked if Doomsday will make everyone cry, Atwell shrugged, mouthed the word 'maybe,' and said, "There's going to be some feelings."

Avengers: Doomsday kicks off the beginning of the end for this chapter of the MCU when it premieres December 18, 2026. A collection of new posters was revealed earlier this week. Next year, the MCU will end the multiverse saga with Avengers: Secret Wars , a movie that MCU boss Kevin Feige has teased will be unlike anything movie watchers have ever seen .

articles.title: CBA breezes into the Class AA state semifinals after routing Valley Central
articles.summary: CBA (12-0) heads to Middletown HS on Nov. 28 vs. Mamaroneck (9-3)
articles.body:
Then, the offense for the Christian Brothers Academy football team actually slowed down during its fourth possession Saturday, as the Brothers required three plays to reach the end zone that time.

The state's No. 3-ranked Class AA squad displayed its overall prowess once again, this time blasting Section 9 champion Valley Central 69-6 in state quarterfinal play at Colonie High School.

CBA (12-0) ran the ball four times during the opening quarter and scored touchdowns on each attempt. In all, the Brothers amassed 263 yards of offense over six plays in the first quarter, which ended with the Brothers ahead 28-0.

"It felt good to play like that," said CBA junior two-way standout Jack Hulett, who was named his team's Offensive Player of the Game. "Coach (Bobby) Burns and the rest of the staff got us prepared pretty well for what we needed to do. We came out and played hard."

The Brothers produced a resounding 61-14 triumph over Saratoga Springs in the Section 2 Class AA Super Bowl to secure a fifth sectional title since 2021. There was absolutely zero letdown Saturday, as CBA senior running back Tommy Toher opened the scoring festivities by dashing 80 yards for a touchdown on the first play from scrimmage. That score started a streak of three consecutive plays from scrimmage that saw the CBA offense score a touchdown.

"Monday, we flipped the script from Saratoga to this game," Hulett said.

"This is a highly motivated group. They are locked in," Burns said. "They want to get back to the (JMA Wireless Dome in Syracuse) for the state final and want to get it done. That is the motivation."

Hulett, a junior who stars at receiver and safety, proceeded to help make it 21-0 as he generated touchdown runs covering 79 and 60 yards, respectively. Toher's second touch of the game resulted in a 4-yard touchdown run with 1:33 left in the first quarter.

The Brothers added four more touchdowns in the second quarter to lead 55-0 at intermission.

"When we execute, we have special players that can do special things," Burns said.

"All the work we have put in is paying off. We are now looking to next week and trying to get better in order to reach the Dome," Hulett said.

The CBA starters had the second half off. The Brothers' reserves moved the ball efficiently over the final 24 minutes, featuring some strong runs by Brady Munsinger and Tyrone Barrow.

Jacob Turner, a sophomore who scooped up a blocked punt and scored a touchdown in the second quarter, returned a kickoff 88 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter.

Toher's opening touchdown run on the first play from scrimmage, followed by Logan Kayser's extra-point boot, ended up being all the offense CBA needed to secure victory.

The Vikings never recovered from seeing the senior running back dash down the left sideline untouched 21 seconds into the game.

Saturday evening's effort offered a number of options for CBA. Hulett touched the ball four times and reached the end zone on three occasions. He ran the ball three times for 162 yards and two touchdowns, and returned an interception 62 yards for a score in the second quarter.

353: CBA's rushing yards on 20 attempts. That figure includes 273 yards on eight carries, including five touchdowns, during the first half.

220: Combined yards on CBA's four return touchdowns. CBA had two scores via interceptions, which covered 62 and 28 yards, one touchdown on a blocked punt return that covered 42 yards and another coming on an 88-yard kickoff return for a touchdown.

4: Interceptions recorded by the Brothers on defense during the first half. In addition to a 62-yard return made by Hulett, senior outside linebacker Myles Johnson brought back a pick in the second quarter for a 28-yard touchdown. Toher and senior defensive back Gunnar Felton also posted interceptions.

Valley Central: The Vikings' improbable run to the state quarterfinals concluded with a 7-5 overall record.

CBA: The Brothers are set to make their fourth trip to the state semifinals since 2022 at Middletown High School next Saturday in a showdown against Section 1 champion Mamaroneck, which defeated Lancaster 20-17. Game time is 6 p.m.
